messages:
maria: Heads-up — prod decode tail latency jumped ~2.3x after the last two rollouts. Short investigation suggests kernel-picker flip + KV cache thrash for long-sequence requests.

sam: Yikes. Where are we seeing the gap (host vs GPU)?

maria: Host-side. Trace shows heavy time in tokenization + request parsing + grpc small writes before any GPU kernel begins. Then GPU runs a smaller kernel path and we see a KV cache miss storm. Miss rate jumped from ~4% to ~28% on the canary shard.

lee: We flipped the kernel picker default to `latency-optimized` for mixed-batch canary on Tuesday. That change biases toward small-kernel implementations at short seqs — could be misclassifying long prompts if the seq histogram isn't used correctly.

sam: Any profiler logs you can paste?

maria: Paste of the important bits:

```
pprof: flame: host_parse 42% | grpc_writev 18% | tokenization_pool 12% | wait_for_kernel 8% | gpu_kernel_small 6% | kv_cache_miss_handler 5%
logs:
[2026-03-20T03:12:11Z] request id=... seq_len=1200 model=gpt-open-v2 preparse=85ms tokenization=40ms grpc_flush=22ms gpu_start_delay=130ms
[2026-03-20T03:12:11Z] kv: miss rate shard=7 -> 0.28 evict_count=432
```

maria: quick ascii flame snippet: `host_parse ===> tokenization ==| grpc_writev -> wait_for_kernel -> small_gpu_kernel` (host work dominates startup).

jon: On SRE side I noticed host CPU run-queue spikes on the same hosts earlier in the day. Tokenization threads pinned causing scheduling pressure.

sam: Could be two orthogonal regressions that amplified: kernel picker chooses a non-optimal kernel for long seqs, and the smaller kernel ends up being more sensitive to KV misses because it triggers different KV access patterns.

lee: Agreed. Immediate mitigations: revert kernel-picker canary or pin selection using `kernel_picker_policy=seq_histogram` for affected routes. Also re-enable `coalesce_writev=true` (we disabled it in the canary).

maria: I ran a bench with seq distribution copied from prod and toggled KV limits: raising per-shard cache cap from 64MB->128MB reduces miss rate in bench to ~6% and removes the eviction spikes. End-to-end tail drops ~45%.

sam: Nice. Any impact on memory? 128MB per shard x 128 shards is non-trivial. Need calc.

maria: Yes — it's ~16GB across shard set. But most hosts have headroom. Propose a targeted increase for the hot shard group rather than cluster-wide bump.

lee: Long-term: change kernel picker to incorporate sequence-length histogram and kv-locality score. Simple heuristic: if P(seq>1024) > 0.05 -> prefer large-seq kernel. Also add an online check that rejects kernel changes if host pre-GPU host-time > 40ms.

sam: Also update batching heuristics: prioritize latency SLO for mixed batches by splitting very long seqs into separate batch windows (deadline-based batching) rather than co-batching with short queries. That avoids pushing long seqs into the small-kernel path.

maria: Repro steps I'm using:
```
# synthetic runner
python tools/load_test.py --concurrency 60 --requests 2000 --seq-dist seq_histogram.json --model gpt-open-v2 --headers "X-Route:longseq-hot"
# tcpdump to capture smallwrite framing
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/trace.pcap port 443 and host <ingress-ip>
```

sam: If coalesce_writev is the other variable, re-enabling it should reduce syscall count and grpc small-write overhead. That plus pinning kernel should give fast signal.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary patch by maria at 1725008000 (includes kernel picker pin + coalesce_writev=true + targeted KV cap bump on hot shards).

maria: I'll run the canary and capture pprof/trace. If the canary looks good we'll stage rollout and open a follow-up to implement the picker improvements and batching change.

jon: SRE will monitor host run-queue, grpc RPS, and kv_evictions metric; will mute alerts until canary completes.

maria: TL;DR: root cause looks like a kernel-selection mismatch for long sequences + KV cache thrash + host-side parsing/grpc small-write overhead. Plan: quick pin + coalesce + targeted cache cap bump for canary, then longer-term picker/batching fixes. cc @sam @lee
